title: XMR to ETH: Does the Receiving Wallet Need ETH Before the Swap?
keyQuestions: Can an empty Ethereum wallet receive ETH?
Can I use a zero-balance wallet for an XMR to ETH swap?
Do I need to activate a new Ethereum wallet first?
Who pays the gas when ETH is sent to my wallet?
Can I receive ETH but still be unable to send the entire balance?
Does the destination network still matter if the address looks correct?
quickSteps: Prepare an Ethereum wallet you control and display its current receiving address.
Verify the XMR to ETH route without treating a zero ETH balance as a requirement to fund the destination first.
Compare the receiving address and required network before sending the source-side Monero payment.
Let the incoming ETH transaction complete before evaluating what the wallet can spend afterward.
Keep enough received ETH available for future gas if you plan to send, swap, bridge, or use the funds on-chain.

issueRouting.start: The Ethereum receiving wallet is empty and you are unsure whether it needs ETH before an XMR to ETH payout.

branches.if: The wallet balance is zero but you control the address and the network matches the active order.
then: Do not fund the wallet merely to activate it.
Use the verified receiving address for the payout.
Wait for the incoming ETH transaction to complete.

branches.if: The address looks correct but you are unsure whether the selected Ethereum network matches the order.
then: Stop before sending the source-side XMR payment.
Verify the destination network separately from the 0x address format.
Use the network required by the active order.

branches.if: The ETH has arrived and you want to send, swap, bridge, or use it on-chain.
then: Treat the next action as a new Ethereum transaction.
Check the expected gas requirement before choosing the outgoing amount.
Keep enough native ETH available to pay the transaction fee.

riskNotes: A zero ETH balance does not mean a normal self-custody Ethereum address cannot receive native ETH.
The sender pays the gas for a standard incoming ETH transfer; the recipient does not need ETH in advance merely to receive it.
A matching 0x address does not prove that the correct EVM network has been selected.
Receiving ETH and spending ETH are separate actions with separate gas requirements.
Trying to send the entire received ETH balance may fail because the outgoing transaction also needs native ETH for gas.
Smart-contract wallets and custodial platforms may have additional operational rules that differ from a standard externally owned Ethereum account.
